candidates.title: The Game
candidates.reason: Nicholas Van Orton accepts an invitation from an opaque entertainment company, then investigates an escalating sequence of apparent accidents, surveillance, betrayals, threats and financial ruin. Across the full 128–129-minute film, each new clue and attempted contact with the organizers changes whether he believes the experience is an elaborate game, a fraud or a real murder plot. The company’s tests, staged television intrusion, apparent accomplices, cemetery abandonment and discovery that a supposed employee is an actor continually reframe the threat; the finale gives a concrete human explanation for the engineered events. The sustained central question, uncertain rules, paranoid reality doubt, investigative pursuit and multiple reversals are strong Mystery fits. Weaknesses: the early setup dwells on Nicholas’s isolation and family history; the explanation is heavily concentrated in the final sequence, and critics question whether the operation could plausibly control so many dangerous contingencies. Its carefully designed dark cinematography remains a strength; the release year is not used as a proxy for visual quality or retro style. No literal supernatural or temporal phenomenon is established.

candidates.title: Frequency
candidates.reason: Homicide detective John Sullivan discovers that his father Frank can answer a radio call from 1969, thirty years before John's present. A warning saves Frank from a fatal fire but changes the history of a serial murderer and puts John's mother in danger. Across the film, father and son investigate the altered Nightingale killings in their respective decades, compare records, transfer physical evidence and identify a suspect, while each intervention changes the present and forces further deductions. The killer's identity and immediate threat receive concrete resolution; the cross-time radio connection is real within the story but its underlying physical mechanism is not rigorously explained. Strong Mystery elements are two linked investigations, progressive changes in evidence and memory, temporal rules, culprit pursuit and sustained suspense. Weaknesses: father-son grief and family reconciliation occupy substantial time; some clues and coincidences are convenient, the serial-killer plot is familiar, and the climactic simultaneous confrontation stretches the time-change logic. The visual assessment reflects the actual production, not its release year.

candidates.title: Fermat's Room
candidates.reason: Four strangers invited to solve an exceptional mathematical puzzle enter a warehouse room whose walls begin to contract whenever they fail to answer timed riddles. Over the complete film they solve successive problems, investigate the mechanism, compare their identities and past connections, find physical evidence of industrial presses, and test competing explanations for who arranged the trap and why. The room's immediate mechanical rules are discovered early, while suspicions about Fermat, an apparent accident, professional jealousy and the guests' concealed relationships shift the suspected motive until the escape and final account. The sustained puzzle work, closed-circle suspicion, confinement and escalating deadlines support a Mystery candidate, though not every individual riddle yields a new explanation of the underlying crime. Weaknesses: several personal/romantic revelations distract from the puzzle, the main motive is held for a late reveal, and contemporary critics found the ending predictable or contrived. Reviewers also describe an uneven low-budget digital presentation and murky dark scenes; those are assessed as observed craft, independently of release year. The threat is engineered rather than supernatural.

research_rejections.title: Exam
research_rejections.reason: Eight applicants try to solve a blank-paper recruitment test under strict rules in a locked room. Their repeated attempts at hidden writing and shifting alliances provide some real puzzle activity, but full-film reconstruction shows that much of the middle focuses on manipulation, coercion, disqualifications and interpersonal conflict rather than cumulative discoveries about the central question. The final answer rests on a tiny wording detail from the opening instructions, while the pharmaceutical-company reveal is largely expository. Substantive criticism, including The Guardian, describes the ending as anticlimactic and the promising setup as underdeveloped. Excluded qualitatively because sustained investigation does not deliver proportionate progressive explanations.
